sources.note: Shazeer et al. 2017 — the sparsely-gated MoE layer, the router, top-k selection, capacity, and the auxiliary loss.
Fedus et al. 2021 — Switch Transformer; top-1 routing and the auxiliary loss form the chapter uses.
Lepikhin et al. 2020 — GShard; top-2 routing and capacity-factor batching.

figures.title: Four experts, one token, top-2
figures.caption: The chapter's four-expert example: x = [1, 2, 0, 0] scores [1, 2, 3, -1] against four router rows, softmax gives [0.089, 0.242, 0.657, 0.012], top-2 picks experts 3 and 2, and renormalizing over the pair gives 0.731 and 0.269. In production, d_model × E = 4,096 × 64 = 262,144 router multiply-adds sit beside 235 million for the selected experts.
figures.alt: A six-stage flow: the input x = [1, 2, 0, 0]; the router matrix W of shape 4 by 4; the scores s = [1, 2, 3, -1]; softmax probabilities [0.089, 0.242, 0.657, 0.012]; top-2 selecting experts 3 and 2; and the weighted sum 0.731 E3 plus 0.269 E2. The note gives the renormalization arithmetic and the production router cost of 262,144 multiply-adds.

data.note: Renormalizing over the selected pair gives 0.657/0.899 = 0.731 and 0.242/0.899 = 0.269. At d_model = 4,096, E = 64, k = 2, the router costs d_model × E = 262,144 multiply-adds per token against 235 million for the two experts, about a tenth of a percent.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to route one token.

steps.label: Read x, the token's hidden vector.
Multiply by the router W: one score per expert.
Combine the two expert outputs and add to the residual.

figures.title: Capacity grows with E; per-token compute grows with k
figures.caption: Per token, the dense FFN costs 2 × 4,096 × 14,336 = 117,440,512 multiply-adds; top-2 routing costs 2 × 2 × 4,096 × 14,336 = 234,881,024. The layer holds 64 × 2 × 4,096 × 14,336 = 7,516,192,768 expert parameters, and 128 experts double that to 15,032,385,536. Capacity grows with E; per-token expert compute grows with k.
figures.alt: Four horizontal bars on a linear scale. Dense FFN 117,440,512; MoE active at k = 2 234,881,024; MoE total at E = 64 7,516,192,768; MoE total at E = 128 15,032,385,536. The active bars are thin slivers beside the totals, and the labels carry the exact counts. The note gives the router's 262,144 multiply-adds and a load example with capacity 640 and 320 dropped assignments.

data.note: d_model = 4,096, d_ff = 14,336, k = 2. Router: 4,096 × 64 = 262,144 multiply-adds, about 0.1% of 235 million. Load example: T = 4,096, E = 8, capacity 640; counts 900, 700, 500, 500, 400, 400, 400, 296 drop 320 assignments (7.8%), and padding is 1,344 of 5,120 expert rows (26%).
